decision.selected_method: matched four-point finite-time passive mechanism interaction study
selected_variables: passive tendon payout offset governing slack-to-taut engagement
segment bending stiffness governing post-engagement compliance

decision.hypothesis: The next uncertainty is why the current symmetric passive mechanism engages but achieves only a 1.36684 stiffness ratio in each direction instead of the fixed 1.5 minimum. Competing hypotheses are: H1, tendon engagement occurs too late because payout slack is excessive, leaving insufficient load range for progressive stiffening; H2, engagement timing is adequate but post-taut structural stiffness is too low. Propose one matched baseline/A/B/A+B finite-time interaction probe on the current candidate, with A a bounded payout-offset reduction and B a bounded segment-bending-stiffness increase.
decision.expected_observation: Under H1, the payout-only point advances the slack-to-taut transition and increases both directional stiffness ratios substantially toward 1.5, while the stiffness-only point has a smaller effect; the combined point adds little beyond payout. Under H2, the stiffness-only point produces the larger reduction in late-stage compliance after engagement, and the combined point may improve beyond either single perturbation. Every point should retain low displacement at least 0.006 m, high displacement at most 0.025 m, residual at most 0.002 m, and the frozen qualification limits.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 is refuted if payout reduction measurably advances engagement but does not improve the stiffness ratio, or drives low displacement below 0.006 m before reaching a ratio of 1.5. H2 is refuted if increased bending stiffness does not change the post-engagement load-displacement slope or stiffness ratio. If neither main effect nor their interaction exceeds numerical variation, both hypotheses are weakened and routing geometry or equilibrium-shape effects become the leading unresolved explanation.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep task T08 unchanged: both plus_x and minus_x programs; force levels, timing, scoring windows, gravity, mount, material coordinate s=0.7, timestep 0.000125 s, passive no-control operation, topology, routing other than the selected payout variable, and every original acceptance and qualification threshold. Use candidate e87a0bff90645b7fe0a4933b9fc6c3dd1d4519984b4bfc4b197ef13b08476a40 as the common baseline. This proposed diagnostic must not substitute for independent numerical confirmation or complete task acceptance.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after the single matched four-point result. Do not select or claim acceptance from it. Use its separate and interaction effects only to decide whether a subsequent explicit design modification should target payout, bending stiffness, both, or neither.
decision.interpretation: Original evidence T08-005-physical-pair reports symmetric stiffness ratios of 1.3668366483436758 and 1.3668366483437635, below 1.5, while low and high displacement, recovery residual, contact, paired-mechanism, and slack-to-taut checks pass. Its acceptance status remains incomplete because independent numerical confirmation is missing, so robustness is UNKNOWN. The proposed four-point action has not run; it is intended to discriminate engagement timing from insufficient post-taut stiffness without changing the frozen task or thresholds.
